reroute_reason: Deliberately did not reroute. The bundle is not mis-routed: dated_t2s_schedule / T2S / settlement / current / role participant is exactly the route topic-index.json lists for this question, and it requires business_date and currency, both of which were supplied. The single needs_context was caused solely by the user's date being a week-date string ('2026-W37-2') rather than a calendar date, and the retriever rejected it with 'Dates must be valid ISO YYYY-MM-DD values.' That is a defect in the request, not in the routing, so it is outside the sanctioned reroute trigger. Rerouting would have required me either to invent a calendar date (the instruction forbids inventing dates) or to substitute t2s_baseline_schedule, which would answer a dated, past-tense question with baseline material - the exact error the case is built to catch. I verified by calendar arithmetic that under ISO 8601 the string resolves to Tuesday 8 September 2026, and I noted in the answer that the library index carries dated-event sections scoped to business date 2026-09-08, but I neither adopted that reading nor retrieved those sections, and I stated nothing about their content.
notes: Checker: 9/9 passed on the first run. Bundle statuses: one retrieval, needs_context, zero sections retrieved. Because nothing was retrieved, the answer deliberately contains no [[section-id]] citation at all (any citation would have been an unknown-citation failure, since there is no evidence to cite) and no clock time whatsoever, no phase names and no schedule values - there is no evidence in this bundle that could support a single time. Key handling: the needs_context status and the retriever's verbatim reason are disclosed in a table; the week-date notation is explained as notation, with the ISO 8601 reading given explicitly as a reasoned inference from calendar convention and explicitly NOT adopted, on three grounds (competing week-numbering conventions, the retriever's YYYY-MM-DD contract, and the cost of dating an operating-day record to the wrong day); the answer separates the two things a dated schedule answer needs (reviewed baseline day structure, which is nominal and never an appointment or a local participant cut-off, and the dated event overlay for that business date and currency) and states that this bundle holds neither; the past tense of the question is addressed directly - it asks for an operating-day record, which only an overlay can supply; and the rule that a routine-only overlay means 'no deviation was published', never 'everything ran on time', is stated as a constraint on any future answer rather than applied to any date here. A short clarification request is given as the system prompt requires for needs_context, with the calendar-date format, the currency scope question, the platform-versus-local-CSD scope question, and the re-ask route in Open items. No external contact is proposed; the fix is entirely in the request.
